title: Loop-Powered Mini Game
summary: Build a mini game that uses loops, variables, and decisions together — your most powerful program yet.

content.title: What You Know Now
content.summary: You now have variables, input, if/else, and for loops — enough to build a real game.
content.body:
Look at everything you can do:

• Variables — store and change information
• input() — ask the player questions
• if / else — make decisions
• for loops — repeat actions automatically
• range() — control exactly how many times

That is enough to build a real interactive game.

content.title: The Project: Dungeon Run
content.summary: Ask for the hero's name, loop through rooms, make decisions in each room, end with a score.
content.body:
You will build a dungeon run game:

1. Ask the player for their hero's name
2. Loop through 5 rooms
3. In each room, something happens (safe, trap, treasure, or boss)
4. After the loop, print a victory message with their name

Here is a starting shape:

name = input("Hero name? ")
for i in range(1, 6):
    print("Room", i, "...")
print(name, "wins!")

content.title: Making It Interesting
content.summary: Use if inside the loop to make different rooms behave differently, and a score variable to track progress.

content.title: Plan Before You Code
content.summary: Decide the rooms, events, and ending before writing a single line.
content.body:
Before writing, answer these questions:

• How many rooms will the player visit?
• Which room numbers are special (trap, treasure, boss)?
• Does the player have HP or a score that changes?
• What does the ending message say?

Your game must use:
- At least one loop
- At least one variable
- At least one if/else
- At least one print that uses a variable

editorPrompt: Build your dungeon run game. Collect the hero's name, loop through at least 5 rooms with different events, and end with a victory message.
starterCode:
# Dungeon Run — Final Project
# Your game needs:
#   - hero name from input()
#   - a loop through at least 5 rooms
#   - at least one special room (trap, treasure, or boss)
#   - a score or HP variable that changes
#   - a victory message at the end

name = input("What is your hero's name? ")
score = 0

# TODO: add your loop here

print("\n" + name + " completed the dungeon! Final score:", score)
progressiveHints: Start with for i in range(1, 6): and just print the room number inside.
Add if i == 3: (or whichever room) to make that room a trap or treasure.
Add score = score + 10 inside the safe rooms, and score = score - 5 for traps.
Don't forget: the print victory message is outside the loop (no indent), so it runs once at the end.
challenge: Add a room where the player finds a secret weapon. Print a special congratulations only if they reach that room AND their score is above 20.
